+**Build the snapshot with a script, never by hand:**
+**Paths in this document are the CONSUMER's layout.** In AI-Handbook itself the
+payload is not installed, so every machinery command here — this one,
+`core/scripts/` instead of `scripts/`. Skills are symlinked and therefore live
+in both repositories; ordinary files under `core/` are not.
+Its inputs are the raw response files themselves, and **nothing about the pull
+request is typed on the command line** — the number, title, body, base and head
+shas all come out of the `get` capture, because a wrong-but-real base sha
+passes every downstream check and then describes a different diff.
+Request the FULL page (`perPage: 100`) for each list. A result too large to
+return inline is written to a path the tool result names, and that path is what
+you pass; a response small enough to return inline has to be written out
+verbatim first — one blob, not field by field. **Pass every page**: a REST page
+holding exactly 100 entries is refused, because only a short page proves the
+list ended, and `complete: true` is an attestation the generator trusts
+**`--fetched-at` is when you called GitHub**, and it is required whenever a
+capture was written by hand. A harness capture's mtime is its fetch time,
+because the harness writes the file as the response arrives; a blob you saved
+from an inline result has an mtime that says when you *saved* it, and a
+response fetched an hour ago but written out just now would sail through the
+freshness gate while missing a reviewer pass. The declaration is bounded: it
+may not be later than the file's mtime, and it may not precede it by more than
+a day. Declaring it early is the safe direction — both gates mean "not older
+than" — so when in doubt, give the earlier time. A mixed batch is the normal
+batch, and needs no special handling: harness captures keep their measured
+mtime and ignore the declaration, which never overwrites a measurement.
+The script derives the snapshot from those files, records each collection's
+files, SHA-256s, capture times and whether each time was measured or declared,
+and `review-loop-record.mjs` re-derives the snapshot from them and refuses
+anything that differs. **So never edit a snapshot — re-run the
+assembler.** A hand-flipped `isResolved` or a paraphrased finding body leaves
+every identifier untouched and has already produced a wrong verdict here once.
+Typing a snapshot is how invented thread ids reached a judge on 2026-09-07.
+**`--threads` is optional, and omitting it is how you run a cheap round
+check.** The round check reads `pr`, `reviews` and `issueComments` and nothing
+else; the generator refuses any snapshot whose `complete.reviewThreads` is not
+explicitly true. So a threads-less snapshot serves the check and can never
+reach a judge as a round that found nothing. In that mode the `get` capture may
+also omit `body` — the body has one reader, the generator's plan-oracle
+resolution, which this snapshot cannot reach. Capture threads (and the body)
+when you are building a record; on a loop with rounds behind it the threads
+payload is usually large enough to land on disk anyway.
+**This matters more than it looks.** A round check costs one small capture set
+per round, and if that set includes a pull request's whole body and every
+review thread, an honest operator transcribing inline responses pays that on
+every round. The discipline that is expensive is the one that gets skipped,
+and skipping it is how a snapshot got fabricated on 2026-09-07.
+The snapshot names its source (`repo`, the `owner/name` this
+checkout declares in `.agents/machinery.json`) and the moment GitHub was read

artifact.patchNote: base...head: the artifact this round's findings are about. This is the diff to read when the rubric asks whether a finding describes a critical flaw. `sinceLastReview.patch` is separate and is normally empty under the write-gate rule, since the judge rules on an already-reviewed head.

budget.artifactDeclaredAtRoundZero: machine-assembled adjudication snapshots: the generator refuses identifiers no captured response contains

dispatch.note: What the dispatch DECLARES, read from the agent definition at the reviewed commit. A verdict receipt's modelRequested/effortRequested are validated against these values. This does NOT establish what the harness served, nor that the checkout the dispatch ran from carried this same definition -- both are stated gaps, not claims.

declineCitation.reason: no tier citation in phase 1a for tier "sensitive"

findings.note: unresolved/resolved is THREAD state, not code state. An unresolved thread may already be fixed and awaiting a reply; isOutdated only tracks whether the anchored hunk moved. Treat these as 'what the reviewer has not yet been told is closed', never as 'what is still broken'.

body: **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the actual per-collection capture times**

Under the documented pr-watch flow, capture files can be fetched earlier and the assembler invoked later, but this default stamps every collection with the invocation time rather than the time GitHub was read. An old capture can therefore pass the one-hour freshness gate, and threads captured before the latest reviewer pass can appear to have been captured after it, defeating `assertCapturedAfterLatestPass` and potentially omitting that pass's findings. Require real per-collection capture timestamps instead of defaulting to `new Date()`. [core/.agents/core/agents-core.mdL98-L103](https://github.com/TheAnswerManIsHere/AI-Handbook/blob/350aed8025fdef84953efb75f726a1ea6a8f8616/core/.agents/core/agents-core.md#L98-L103)
Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Source the artifact base SHA from GitHub's captured PR**

When `--base` contains the wrong local 40-character commit, the downstream endpoint check only verifies that the object exists, so the erroneous value still controls `artifactDiff`, artifact size, territory classification, and plan-file discovery. Because this assembler reconstructs the PR object from operator-supplied flags rather than the captured `get` response, those outputs can describe a different diff while looking fully validated; read and provenance-bind the base SHA from GitHub instead. [core/.agents/core/agents-core.mdL109-L114](https://github.com/TheAnswerManIsHere/AI-Handbook/blob/350aed8025fdef84953efb75f726a1ea6a8f8616/core/.agents/core/agents-core.md#L109-L114)
Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not attest single-page arrays as complete**

When `get_reviews` or `get_comments` exceeds the documented `perPage: 100`, this CLI accepts only one capture file for each collection, performs no pagination check for either array, and nevertheless sets both completeness attestations to `true`. `fromMcp` trusts those flags, so later pages—including clean-pass issue comments—are silently omitted and the adjudication can undercount spent rounds; support concatenating multiple page captures or refuse unless completion is established. This behavior is propagated to every consumer of the payload.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match identifiers as complete JSON values**

When an invented numeric identifier is a substring of unrelated capture text, `text.includes(id)` accepts it even though the capture never returned that identifier—for example, snapshot id `234` passes a capture containing only `{"id":12345}`, and id `0` passes almost any realistic response. Since the other validators permit numeric IDs and self-consistent fabricated URLs, this leaves the new provenance guarantee bypassable; compare exact parsed identifier fields or at least delimiter-bounded serialized values. [core/.agents/core/agents-core.mdL111-L114](https://github.com/TheAnswerManIsHere/AI-Handbook/blob/350aed8025fdef84953efb75f726a1ea6a8f8616/core/.agents/core/agents-core.md#L111-L114)
Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify each thread's content and state against its capture**

When a snapshot is edited or reconstructed after assembly, changing a thread's `isResolved`, body, or path—or pairing a valid comment with a different valid thread—leaves every identifier somewhere in the unchanged capture, so this check still passes. `buildRecord` then presents those fields as GitHub-derived and uses them for unresolved counts, the adjudicator's finding text, and territory classification; compare each normalized entry structurally with the parsed capture, or otherwise bind the generated snapshot itself to the capture, rather than validating only the identifier set. [core/.agents/core/agents-core.mdL98-L103](https://github.com/TheAnswerManIsHere/AI-Handbook/blob/350aed8025fdef84953efb75f726a1ea6a8f8616/core/.agents/core/agents-core.md#L98-L103)
Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refuse captures without a review_threads collection**

When the threads capture is an API error object, an old snapshot-format array, or any object lacking `review_threads`, this fallback silently converts it to an empty thread list and then marks that list complete. The identifier check is vacuous for the resulting empty array, so `review-loop-record.mjs` can accept the capture as a clean round with zero findings; validate that the raw response contains a `review_threads` array before normalizing it. [core/.agents/core/agents-core.mdL98-L103](https://github.com/TheAnswerManIsHere/AI-Handbook/blob/350aed8025fdef84953efb75f726a1ea6a8f8616/core/.agents/core/agents-core.md#L98-L103)
Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make the assembler command runnable in this repository**

When the live, symlinked `pr-watch` skill is used in AI-Handbook itself, this newly documented command exits with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`: `scripts/snapshot-from-captures.mjs` does not exist here, while the implementation exists only at `core/scripts/snapshot-from-captures.mjs`. Because ordinary files under `core/` are not activated here like skills are, the mandatory “never by hand” snapshot route cannot be followed in this repository; provide a root-aware invocation or wrapper while preserving the consumer path.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require proof that all thread pages were supplied**

When a thread capture omits `pageInfo`, or the caller supplies only the terminal page of a multi-page response, `hasNextPage` is absent or false and this condition accepts the capture before emitting `complete.reviewThreads: true`. The payload's `totalCount` is ignored, so even `{ "totalCount": 250, "review_threads": [] }` is accepted as a complete zero-thread round, understating findings and potentially producing a stop verdict; require an explicit terminal `pageInfo` and reconcile the concatenated count with `totalCount` before attesting completeness. This defect propagates with the machinery to every consumer.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the fetch time for inline captures**

When an API result is returned inline, the skill instructs the agent to write that blob to disk afterward, so this mtime records the later save time rather than when GitHub was read. An hours-old response copied immediately before assembly therefore passes the one-hour freshness gate and can appear to postdate a reviewer pass whose findings it cannot contain. Fresh evidence after the earlier timestamp fix is that the amended `agent-written` flow still dates these captures solely from save-time mtime; persist the actual fetch time with the capture or refuse when it cannot be established.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add the synced-payload ownership warning**

When this new script is vendored into a consumer as `scripts/snapshot-from-captures.mjs`, it lacks the standard `SYNCED FROM AI-Handbook` warning carried by the other machinery files, even though the machinery blocker records that this warning is present on every delivered file. An agent can therefore edit this ordinary-looking consumer copy and have that work silently overwritten by the next sync; add the language-appropriate ownership notice immediately after the shebang.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refuse thread captures that omit comments**

When a captured thread has `comments` missing or null, this default converts the malformed entry to `comments: []`; that bypasses `assertMcpSnapshotShape`, which was specifically written to reject a thread with no comments array. The thread still satisfies `totalCount`, but `flattenMcpThreads` and `reviewerFindings` silently drop it, so a real finding can become a clean round and affect the adjudicator's verdict. Refuse the raw thread instead of normalizing the missing collection to empty; because this script is fleet-vendored under `core/`, the false-clean behavior reaches every consumer.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record each collection's actual fetch time**

When inline collections are fetched sequentially, this applies one shared `fetchedAt` value to all of them. If threads were fetched first, a reviewer pass landed, and reviews were fetched later, supplying the later call time stamps the stale threads as postdating that pass, so `assertCapturedAfterLatestPass` accepts a snapshot that cannot contain its findings. Fresh evidence after the earlier timestamp fix is that the amended flow still feeds the same scalar to every collection; accept per-file/per-collection times or conservatively bind all captures to the earliest fetch. This behavior is propagated to every consumer.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require a total count for terminal thread captures**

When a `get_review_comments` capture omits `totalCount` and the caller supplies only a terminal page, `pageInfo.hasNextPage: false` passes and this branch sets `total` to null, skipping the only check that any earlier pages were included before `complete.reviewThreads: true` is emitted. Fresh evidence after the claimed pagination fix is the explicit support for count-less payloads, so a terminal-only capture can still understate findings and produce a stop verdict; require `totalCount` or another verifiable proof that the concatenated pages cover the whole collection. This fail-open path ships to every consumer.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify REST pagination starts at page one**

When the caller accidentally supplies only a later short page from `get_reviews` or `get_comments`, this check accepts it because it examines only the final page's length, then the assembler attests the truncated array as complete. Fresh evidence after the multi-page fix is that no page number, first-page marker, or total count is checked, so omitted earlier reviews or clean-pass comments silently reduce the round count; require capture metadata proving an ordered sequence beginning at page 1 before setting completeness.
